newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Silver Grant says ignorant of JV forecast.
newsitem.headline: Silver Grant says ignorant of JV forecast.

text.p: Silver Grant International Industries Ltd said it did not know of the publication of a profit forecast by a joint venture unit and was investigating the matter.

In a statement published on Wednesday, the company said that the forecast, which indicated an expected profit growth of 20 percent for its joint venture Beijing Wang Fu Jing Retail Management Co Ltd for 1997, were made by the JV company without prior consultation with Silver Grant directors.
Silver Grant has a 50 percent stake in Beijing Wang Fu Jing.
The brochure containing the forecast had not been reviewed by auditors or financial advisors of the company, it said.

"The directors of the company are investigating the cause of the publication of such unsubstantiated statements and shall take the necessary steps to ensure that the publication of unsubstantiated statements of this nature shall not occur in future," the statement said.

The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Ltd has expressed grave concern over the publication of the unsubstantiated statement and has indicated that it reserves the right to take further action, if necessary, Silver Grant said.
Silver Grant and Beijing Wangfujing Department Store (Group) Co Ltd, which is listed in Shanghai, set up the equally-owned Sino-foreign joint venture in October 1996.

The joint venture company is a management company overseeing various businesses engaged in the processing, packaging, food catering, and entertainment businesses related to department stores and shopping malls in Beijing, Shanghai, Chengdu, Guangzhou, and Wuhan.
Silver Grant is 10 percent held by China Construction Bank and about 15 percent held by China National Non-Ferrous Metal Industries Corp (CNNC).
Trading in shares of Silver Grant, which was suspended on Tuesday, resumed on Wednesday. The shares ended HK$0.25 higher at HK$4.60 at the midday break on Wednesday.
